reuse.why: Builds on the tree's getExpectedAmount/getScheduledAmount, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, and computes the API field via getScheduledAmount; schedule-template now calls the shared helper instead of its own midpoint.

duplication.why: The rule itself lives once in getExpectedAmount; schedule-template still keeps its own isbetween/isapprox dispatch in front of a helper that already handles every op, and the null-to-0 guards stay repeated at call sites.

placement.why: The rule is in shared/schedules.ts and the field in the API schedule model; putting expectedAmount in scheduleModel.toExternal exposes it on every schedule conversion, not only the list, and makes the input type carry a read-only field.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule amounts and the API field, with tests and release notes; stale comments ('rounded midpoint') are left at several call sites.

maintainability.why: A single helper with an op argument is easy to own, but the redundant op dispatch in schedule-template, an op threaded through after an unused inverse flag, desktop callers (Balance, schedule lists) left without the op, and outdated comments make the rule's reach unclear.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts decides itself which ops go through getExpectedAmount (isbetween || isapprox) instead of passing every amount and op to it.

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold; the only repeat is the call-site op dispatch in schedule-template, which is plain rather than disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount each gain an op parameter and getExpectedAmount an isapprox branch; schedule-template createScheduleList keeps its own op dispatch around the helper.
